headline: The magnetic sub-test was not the clean test either side registered, and one of our own pre-registered falsifiers (OBS-O-02) fired to say so. The dome's own Kp<2 precondition failed (Kp 2.333), and so did its own operational quiet test (Boulder Z daily stdev 7.62 nT against its < 5 nT rule - though no day in the preceding month passed that test either). Evaluated anyway, under one post-hoc detectability rule applied to both sides: on the dome's named Z component its signature contact-phase timing (peaks at first and last contact) is absent at all six priority stations, where a dome-sized -17 nT signal would have stood 4-30 times above the noise under every pulse width and trend model we tried - and would still have been detectable at the dome formula's own smaller per-station amplitudes. Its -17 to -21 nT range is also absent at every station with more than 80% coverage, by the dome's own coverage table or by ours. The dome formula's smaller Boulder-baseline amplitudes (about -7 to -13 nT) under obscuration-shaped timing are a different matter: detectable only in some analysis variants (with a quadratic trend they are absent at 5 of 6 priority stations; with the primary linear-trend fit power is 0.24-0.84), so we treat that part of the claim as not robustly tested. The same rule treats our own range the same way: the upper part of our registered -5 to -25 nT band is refuted as-if, the lower part untested, and under the metric we actually pre-registered our band was met on the eclipse day and on 17 of 30 ordinary days - non-diagnostic, our design error. One test we pre-registered on the review site (not in the OTS file) went the dome's way: across the dome's stations the small Z residuals scale with the dome's FSF profile better than with our binary magnetic-latitude profile, more strongly than on any of 19 control days - but the same day shows latitude-scaled Z structure of similar or larger size two hours after the eclipse, so we do not attribute it to the eclipse or to FSF physics. Our Hartland obscuration claim (88%) failed; the true value was 94.4%. That is our error (erratum ECLIPSE-2026-08-12-ERRATUM-1), not a failure of standard physics. The geometric result (294 km path vs the dome's 1.3 km) stands.

SR-1_kp_gate.text: One rule for both sides. Every pre-registered criterion that carries a Kp<2 precondition - ours (B1-M-001, OBS-D-02, OBS-D-04, OBS-S-02) and the dome's (PRED-095 'IF Kp<2', Tier-1 'falsification only on verified Kp<2 day', Tier-3 'Kp<2 entire Aug 9-12', live countdown 'Requires Kp < 2') - is formally UNTESTED: GFZ definitive Kp was 2.333 for 18-21 UT on 2026-08-12 and 3.0 for 15-18 UT on 2026-08-11. Note the dome text also leaves Kp 2-3 unspecified: 'IF Kp >= 3, signal will be buried in storm noise (not a falsification)' (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:74) while validity requires Kp<2 (:91); 2.333 falls in the gap.
SR-1_kp_gate.note: Applies preconditions that WERE pre-registered (ours in the frozen file, the dome's in its published text); the post-hoc part is the decision to apply them identically to both sides.

DR-1_detectability_override.text: Beyond the formal status, a prediction is scored 'as-if' ONLY for the part of its predicted amplitude that exceeds 3 x the empirical null SD of the same metric on the same UT window, estimated from the preceding 30 days with Kp(12-24 UT) <= 3 (i.e. at noise levels comparable to or worse than the eclipse day). The same rule is applied to our ranges and to the dome's. Below that threshold a claim is 'untested at this noise level', not confirmed and not refuted. Detection power for a -17 nT signal was checked by injection into real control-day noise (per-station table in z_component_evaluation).
DR-1_detectability_override.note: Post hoc. Kept physically separate from the scoring of pre-registered criteria; never re-words a frozen criterion.
DR-1_detectability_override.rev3_sensitivity: Threshold varied 2/3/5 sigma in z_component_evaluation.sensitivity_table. The contact-phase conclusion survives every variant; the obscuration-shaped conclusion at -17 nT survives 2 and 3 sigma at all six priority stations and weakens at 5 sigma (power 0.24 at HAD, 0.56 at ESK, 0.58 at EBR).

DQ-1_publication_state.text: A station is excluded from every absolute-baseline (protocol-metric) criterion if the 16-20 UT median H of its quiet-day set spans more than 50 nT (about 3x the largest span, 16 nT, at any station). Only GUI trips it (~185 nT step between July quasi-definitive and August variation files). Applied uniformly to OBS-D-02 counts, PRED-095 tallies, B1-M-001, B2-M-001/002 and OBS-O-01. Offset-immune template fits are unaffected and are still reported for GUI.
DQ-1_publication_state.note: Post hoc. Kept physically separate from the scoring of pre-registered criteria; never re-words a frozen criterion.

CTL-1_control_stations.text: Any candidate eclipse feature is checked against non-eclipsed observatories with the SAME template and window: ASC (Ascension, zero obscuration, Sun 13 to -1 deg over 18-19 UT, dayside), KOU (Kourou, zero obscuration, full daylight), HER (Hermanus, zero obscuration, NIGHT side after ~16:15 UT - correcting the cycle-1 review, which described HER as dayside). A feature that a non-eclipsed control reproduces at similar z is not attributed to the eclipse.
CTL-1_control_stations.note: Post hoc. Kept physically separate from the scoring of pre-registered criteria; never re-words a frozen criterion.

dome_own_quiet_test_BOU_stdev.dome_rule: "Eclipse magnetic signal IS real but requires quiet geomagnetic conditions (BOU stdev < 5 nT) to detect" (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:67-68); dome labels 2016-03-09 QUIET (BOU std 2.23 nT), 2024-04-08 MODERATE (5.59), 2017-08-21 STORM (8.05) (:55-58). dome_own_quiet_test_BOU_stdev.reproduction: The dome's three published values are reproduced to 0.01 nT by one definition: standard deviation of BOU 1-min Z over the whole UT day, no detrending ([2.23, 8.05, 5.59] vs published [2.23, 8.05, 5.59]). No other definition we tried comes within 0.1 nT.
dome_own_quiet_test_BOU_stdev.result: FAILS the dome's quiet test (7.62 > 5 nT) - by the dome's own operational criterion, 2026-08-12 was not a quiet day.
dome_own_quiet_test_BOU_stdev.control_context: None of the 30 preceding days passes either: BOU Z daily stdev ranged 5.49-15.21 nT, including 6.4 nT on 2026-07-19 (Kp max 1.0) and 10.52 nT on 2026-08-06 (Kp max 1.0). In July-August the statistic is dominated by the daytime Sq variation at Boulder, not by disturbance, so the test cannot certify ANY summer day as quiet.
dome_own_quiet_test_BOU_stdev.reading_for_both_sides: For the dome: its own precondition was not met, so by its own terms the magnetic test is void (this strengthens Option B). Against the dome: as operationalised, the quiet test would void a Northern-summer eclipse regardless of geomagnetic activity, i.e. it functions as an unconditional escape clause for this event (this is the concern behind Option A). We report both; we do not use either reading to score a prediction.

methods.data: INTERMAGNET 1-minute data via BGS GIN web service (https://imag-data.bgs.ac.uk/GIN_V1/GINServices, publicationState=best-avail, per-day requests), 2026-07-13..2026-08-12. H = recorded H, or sqrt(X^2+Y^2) for XYZ-reporting observatories. Fetched 2026-09-26.
methods.obscuration: Computed, not taken from the NASA web calculator: skyfield 1.55 + JPL DE421 topocentric apparent Sun/Moon, WGS84 station coordinates from IAGA-2002 headers, area-overlap of the solar disc at 1-min cadence 15:00-21:00 UT. Validation: greatest eclipse reproduced at 17:45 UT at 65.225N/25.228W with obscuration 1.0 (NASA 17:45:53.8); 2017-08-21 Boulder max at 17:46 UT, 93.6% (matches published local circumstances within ~1 pp). Deviation from the protocol (which named the NASA local-circumstances calculator) is disclosed; an independent NASA-calculator cross-check is recommended before publication.
methods.quiet_days: Protocol step 2 read as: days with max 3-h Kp <= 1 in the 30 days preceding the event, ties/fill by lowest daily Kp sum. Only 4 days satisfy max Kp<=1 (07-19, 07-20, 08-01, 08-06); 5th filled with 08-05 (sum 3.33). Sensitivity set ranked purely by daily sum: 08-06, 08-05, 08-07, 07-19, 08-01. Baseline = per-UT-minute mean over quiet days (finer than the protocol's "same UT-hour"; the difference is sub-nT for this window).
methods.protocol_metric: Peak = max |signed deviation| in +/-60 min around each station's computed max-coverage minute (exact protocol step 2).
methods.supplementary_metric_NOT_PREREGISTERED: Eclipse-isolating detrend: fit a line to the deviation over [first contact-60 min, first contact] and [last contact, last contact+60 min], subtract, report mean residual over [t_max-30, t_max+30]. Empirical null = the same statistic on the same UT windows on every non-quiet day of the preceding 30 days with Kp(15-21UT) <= 2.67 (n=13-19 per station). Sensitivity: anchor 30 vs 60 min, linear vs quadratic.
methods.components: H (our frozen protocol's component) AND Z (the dome's named Tier-1 instrument, monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:107). Both use the same quiet-day per-minute baseline. X/Y/F are available in the scripts but not scored (the dome's pattern clause is moot once amplitude fails).
methods.quiet_days_interpretation: 'Kp <= 1' in protocol step 2 is read as max 3-h GFZ Kp <= 1.0; 1+ (1.333) does NOT qualify. Four days satisfy it (07-19, 07-20, 08-01, 08-06); 08-05 (max Kp 1.333 in 12-24 UT but lowest daily sum 3.33 among the rest) fills the fifth slot per the tie/fill rule. EBR, CLF, BEL and SFS use 4 days because their 2026-08-01 files contain no valid samples 15-21 UT (data gaps); no day was dropped for publication state.
methods.leave_one_out: For control-day statistics the day being evaluated is removed from its own baseline (leave-one-out) so quiet days are not compared with themselves.
methods.joint_template_fit_NOT_PREREGISTERED: Replaces the cycle-1 window-mean detrend as the primary eclipse-isolating metric (the window-mean compared a mean to peak predictions and attenuated lagged signals). Model over [local C1-60, local C4+60]: dev(t) = a + b t + A s(t), with s(t) a template normalised to peak 1, so A is directly a PEAK-equivalent amplitude in nT with the trend fitted simultaneously. Templates: obscuration(t) passed through a first-order recovery lag tau = 0, 15, 30, 60 min; local C1/C4 contact-phase (Gaussians, sigma 10 min, at each station's own first and last contact); global C1/C4 contact-phase (16:59 and 21:01 UT, the contact times in the dome's own post_eclipse_analysis() code, monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:191-195), window 15:59-22:01. Injection into real control-day noise recovers A at 100% for all tau (linear model).
methods.window_mean_detrend_retained_as_sensitiv: The cycle-1 metric is kept only as a sensitivity check. Injection-recovery of its window mean (signal peak-normalised): 100% at tau 0, 95% at 15 min, 83% at 30 min, 61% at 60 min; window-mean/peak ratio ~0.65-0.72. The pre-contact-only extrapolation variant has null SD 6-15 nT and is non-informative (table in per_station).
methods.correlation_tests: Pearson r between the linearly-detrended deviation and each template over the same windows, reproducing the dome's r > 0.7 (success) / r > 0.5 (falsification) thresholds, with the same statistic computed on every control day for a false-positive rate.

z_component_evaluation.why: Curmudgeon critical hole: the dome's Tier-1 claim names the INTERMAGNET 1-min Z component, pattern Z down, correlated with 'umbra contact geometry', and separately claims peaks at C1 and C4, not at maximum (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:104-109). Its 2026-03-15 revision instead says 'Z minimum within 30 minutes of maximum eclipse coverage' (:72-73), and its own analysis code correlates against GLOBAL contact times 16:59 / 21:01 UT (:191-195). We evaluate all three readings on Z so the result does not depend on picking one.

The minimum does fall within 30 min of max coverage at most stations, but a timing hit on its own is weak (about half of any +/-60 min window lies within +/-30 min) and the depth is 13-21 nT short of -17..-21 at every priority station.

obscuration_shaped_fit.result: Z joint-fit amplitudes with an obscuration template (tau 0) are negative at every priority station: EBR -6.1 (z -1.4), SPT -4.0 (z -1.3), HAD -5.5 (z -1.7), CLF -2.8 (z -0.8), NGK -3.6 (z -1.2), ESK -7.6 (z -2.4) nT - the dome's 'Z down' sign, at roughly a quarter to a third of its amplitude. BUT the non-eclipsed dayside control ASC gives -2.5 (z -2.1), -2.0 (z -1.8), -5.0 (z -3.1), -4.3 (z -2.9), -5.3 (z -3.2), -5.9 (z -3.2) nT with the same templates, so the negative-Z shape is common to stations the eclipse never touched and is not attributed to the eclipse (CTL-1).
obscuration_shaped_fit.rev3_quadratic_trend: With a quadratic trend in the joint fit (C2-4c) the tau-0 Z amplitudes shrink to EBR -2.5, SPT +0.1, HAD -1.3, CLF -1.1, NGK -4.2, ESK -4.9 nT, and the non-eclipsed ASC control with the same templates goes to EBR +0.2, SPT +0.4, HAD -1.6, CLF -1.1, NGK -1.9, ESK -2.1 nT. Most of the rev2 'Z-down shape' at the priority stations and at ASC was late-afternoon curvature absorbed by a linear-trend fit, as the cycle-2 review suspected. NGK (-4.2, z -2.4) and ESK (-4.9, z -2.6) keep a residual under the quadratic model; ASC with the NGK/ESK templates keeps -1.9/-2.1 (z -2.0/-2.1). Not attributed to the eclipse.
obscuration_shaped_fit.LER_disclosure: LER (dome-cited, not a Tier-1 priority station, ephemeris obscuration 0.88) has the largest tau-0 Z fit of any station: -12.82 nT (null mean 0.91, SD 5.16, z -2.66) with a linear trend - within about one null SD of -17 nT, where power was only 0.6. With a quadratic trend it is -5.97 nT (z -1.85). Its raw Z minimum in the +/-60 min window is only -3.42 nT, so the fit amplitude is driven by window-scale curvature. At both of the dome's global contact times (16:59 and 21:01 UT) H dropped 2-6 nT at NGK, WNG, BEL and LER. The 16:59 drop came before the eclipse reached those stations - which is what the dome's global-contact (R3) reading predicts, and we no longer count it against the dome (C2-1). On that day's activity level the double coincidence occurs for ~13% of arbitrary time pairs (4.7% on an average control day); it is absent on Z; amplitudes are a quarter or less of the dome's; the r > 0.7 template test does not fire.
NGK's global-contact H fit (-7.8 nT, z -2.5) is within 2 nT of the dome's frozen NGK central (-6.67). One station of seven.
Z-down obscuration-shaped fits at all six priority stations (-2.8 to -7.6 nT). The sign matches the dome's pattern clause; the non-eclipsed ASC shows the same shape (-2.0 to -5.9 nT).
Lagged H fits at EBR and SPT (-8.5 / -8.8 nT at tau 30) sit near the dome's frozen EBR/SPT centrals (-10.66 / -9.82). Hermanus, with no eclipse, gives -8.8 / -9.5 with the same templates.

LER's linear-trend obscuration-shaped Z fit is -12.8 nT (z -2.7), within about one null SD of the dome's -17 nT and close to its BOU-formula central (-9.5). Power at LER was low (0.60) and a quadratic trend halves it (-6.0), but on the linear model it is the one station where a PRED-095-sized Z signal cannot be ruled out.

WIN-010 site-registered profile test: on Z the small eclipse-window residuals follow the dome's FSF profile better than our binary magnetic-latitude profile at every alpha and coverage input, and the eclipse day's FSF-scale significance exceeds every one of 19 control days. We attribute it to a latitude-scaled external field (larger at +2 h with no eclipse), not to FSF physics - but our own profile lost this test.

By the dome's own operational quiet test (BOU Z daily stdev < 5 nT, which we reproduce exactly from its three published values), 2026-08-12 was not quiet (7.62 nT). On its own terms the dome is entitled to call the magnetic test void.

self_corrections.finding: Our range was drawn from daytime-eclipse ensembles and not scaled for a near-sunset eclipse (Sun 5-14 deg at maximum). The data cannot confirm it: the protocol metric 'hits' it on ordinary days, the eclipse-attributable fits that reach the -5..-12 nT part of the range are reproduced at a non-eclipsed control, and the lower part of the range is below that day's detectability. The observed residuals are compatible with the low end of our range under a lagged-recovery model and with zero. The cycle-1 statement that no station showed a >= 5 nT dip came partly from comparing a window mean with a peak range, and is withdrawn.

Standard Sq physics gives a latitude-dependent sign relative to the Sq current focus; a uniform negative sign for all European stations was over-specified. Descriptively, cycle-1 detrended residuals were negative south of about 45N (EBR, SPT, SFS, GUI, SUA) and weakly positive north of about 49N (ESK, HAD, NGK, MAB, DOU, WNG, BEL), with LER and CLF as exceptions. The boundary was noticed after the fact and the stations share a common external field, so this is reported descriptively, not as evidence.

kernel_of_truth: Two real things sit under the dome's eclipse claims. First, eclipses really do disturb ground magnetometers, and on 2026-08-12 the raw readings at the dome's stations really were 13-19 nT low - a defender looking only at those numbers would see a hit. Second, the dome's insistence on a quiet-day (Kp<2) precondition is good practice, and this day failed it. Both are true, and by the dome's own Boulder quiet test the day was not quiet either. Neither saves the claim: ordinary days produce the same raw numbers, the dome's own named component shows nothing near its amplitude, its signature contact-phase timing is absent where it would have stood out clearly, and the only eclipse-shaped features we could find also appear at observatories the eclipse never reached. A void test is not a confirmation, and 47 days later the dome's own live scoreboard still reads PENDING.

WIN_010_profile.registration: data/wins.json id=010 detail_verdict_text (pre-event wording): residual (observed delta_Z)/(baseline x coverage^alpha), alpha in {0.5,0.8,1.0,1.2,1.5}; does it track the dome FSF profile or a magnetic-latitude profile (CGM 30-50 deg in-band = ensemble-median signal; HAD/ESK/LER out-of-band <= 30% of it; NGK marginal)? WIN_010_profile.method: Observed delta_Z = eclipse-attributable Z joint-fit amplitude (A - null_mean), obscuration template tau 0 (tau 30 and quadratic trend as sensitivity), 8 evaluable stations (COI no data; GUI included because the template fit is offset-immune). Baseline -10.9 nT (the W004 baseline only rescales and cannot change the ranking). Each profile is fitted with one free scale k by weighted least squares (weights from each station's null SD); the profile with lower chi2 "tracks more tightly". CGM latitudes from the WIN-010 prose (centred dipole, IGRF-14 2020 pole). Implementation choices (WLS scale fit, chi2 comparison) are post hoc: the registration did not specify a statistic.
WIN_010_profile.result_Z_summary: On Z the dome FSF profile beats our binary magnetic-latitude profile at every alpha, under both coverage inputs, on all 8 stations and on the pre-registered discriminating subset (LER/HAD/ESK/GUI), and with tau 30 or a quadratic trend. At alpha 1, dome coverage: FSF scale k = 0.524 (k/se 4.51), chi2 4.77 vs 13.39 for the binary profile. The ranking is stable across alpha in [0.5,1.5] - by our own pre-registered rule the discrimination is 'robust', and it goes against our profile: the out-of-band stations ESK and LER carry the LARGEST negative residuals, not suppressed ones.
WIN_010_profile.result_H_summary: On H (check): non-discriminating - the winner flips with the metric variant (binary profile wins tau 0 linear; FSF wins with a quadratic trend on all 8 stations but not on the discriminating subset; binary wins tau 30), and the eclipse-day statistics sit inside the control-day distribution.

controls.control_days: Same test on the 19 control days with all 8 stations evaluable and Kp(12-24 UT) <= 3 (Z, tau 0, alpha 1, dome coverage): FSF beats the binary profile on 12 of 19 ordinary days, but no control day reaches the eclipse day's FSF scale significance (k/se 4.32; control days >= that: 0 of 19; |k/se| >= : 1 of 19). Quadratic trend: event k/se 2.57, control days >= : 0 of 19. H: event inside the control distribution (13 of 19 control days have |k/se| >= the event).
controls.time_shift: Same test on the eclipse day with every station's template and window shifted in time: -240/-180/-120 min give FSF k/se -0.68/-1.58/-1.16 (nothing before the eclipse); +120 min gives -6.31 (chi2 25.01) - latitude-scaled Z structure of LARGER size and opposite sign two hours after the eclipse, when no station was eclipsed. The eclipse-day evening Z field carries strong latitude-scaled external structure (storm-recovery day, Kp 2.333); the in-window result is plausibly its leading edge.
controls.leave_one_out: Dropping any one station leaves FSF k/se between 3.78 and 4.34 (linear trend); no single station drives it.

WIN_010_profile.scored_result: DOME-FAVOURABLE against our pre-registered binary magnetic-latitude profile on Z; NOT attributable to the eclipse. Our binary profile (out-of-band <= 30%) is disfavoured at every alpha. The FSF profile tracks the residuals better, but FSF (proportional to tan of geographic latitude) is also a proxy for any latitude-increasing external field (geographic and CGM latitude correlate at r = 0.991 across these stations, WIN-010 prose), and the time-shift control shows such a field was present on the day at larger amplitude with no eclipse. We therefore do not read it as evidence for FSF physics, but we do not claim it for standard physics either.
WIN_010_profile.failure_attribution_note: Our side of this test failed: the binary <=30% out-of-band suppression profile was our own first-order stand-in (self-described in the WIN-010 prose as lacking a paper-tabulated attenuation factor), and its stated basis (Kim & Chang 2018) is itself under the ISS-3101 citation review (erratum E-2). This is a failure of our representation of standard physics, not a demonstrated failure of the Sq mechanism. The dome side is not credited with a confirmation because the controls show a non-eclipse cause.
